claims: If a business hires you primarily for your labour ... they may be required to pay the SG super guarantee on your behalf.
whys: The same page states the rule definitively in contractor-pay-calculator-content.tsx line 239 ('that business must pay super on your behalf'). Under the SG Act, a contract wholly or principally for labour makes the business liable for SG. The FAQ answer (also used in the FAQPage JSON-LD) is softer than the page body. I did not change the modality.

claims: Unbilled time, insurance and sick days are why many contractors charge 1.4 to 1.6 times the employee rate.
whys: This is a population claim with no source ('many contractors'). The same 1.4 to 1.6 rule of thumb appears at line 95. It is the lead of the 'What Rate Should I Charge?' section and is also in the FAQPage schema.

claims: Workers' compensation is compulsory in some states for contractors who employ others.
whys: Every state and territory makes workers' compensation insurance compulsory for employers, so 'in some states' looks wrong. The answer also opens with a population claim that cites no source ('Most contractors carry 3 types of insurance'). The premium ranges ($300 to $1,200, $400 to $2,000) and 'required for consultants, accountants, and IT professionals' are unsourced too. Professional indemnity is a legal requirement for some professions, such as registered tax agents, but not for all consultants or IT contractors.

claims: If you're under $75,000, GST registration is optional.
whys: Taxi and ride-sourcing drivers must register for GST whatever their turnover. The page body says so (contractor-pay-calculator-content.tsx, GST Registration and BAS Lodgement paragraph). The FAQ states the rule with no exception. Separately, the content paragraph says 'turnover exceeding $75,000' while the FAQs say '$75,000 or more' (ATO wording is $75,000 or more).
constants: GST registration threshold ($75,000) is hard-coded in prose; it could come from a GST constant

whys: The figure 48 is typed into the prose and into DAY_RATE_GROSS (line 33: 1_000 * 5 * 48). BILLABLE_WEEKS = 48 already exists in the same file. If BILLABLE_WEEKS changes, the prose and this number will drift apart.
SummaryRow divides by weeks / 2 without flooring. When weeks per year is odd (for example 47), the footnote says 23 fortnights while the code uses 23.5. The footnote and the calculation disagree.
constants: Code: use weeksPerYear / 2 in the footnote, or floor it in SummaryRow
